reasoning: All five actual defects are technical, and none is artistic. D1 is a spoken-word integrity failure, so the take is unusable. D2 is caption fit with no measured passing caption set. D3 is event timing against fixed documentary limits. D4 is a direction text that put the failing word into synth-facing fields, an exposure I accepted in v3 and which may have materialized. D5 is a soundcheck threshold that let a content-word substitution through. v4 corrects D4 narrowly and is otherwise v3. Board v3 is arithmetically sound, and take 6 suggests its caps hold, though n1 is nearly at its cap. I still would not spend a final take on these exact bytes yet, for three reasons. First, the TTS allowance is spent (12 of 12), so any take needs new capacity, and it should go to the path most likely to pass. Second, the beat mechanism itself is unproven. Take 6 never reached segmentation, and nothing measured shows the twelve beats landing where the captions need them. Third, word-level failures recur regardless of the direction mechanism, so v4 does not meet the recurrence requirement. Measuring take 6's speech runs costs nothing and settles which path to take. With a one-take-only budget, a script correction is the better alternative only if take 6 shows the beats did not land. It does not reduce random word risk by itself, but it removes the dependence on twelve uncontrolled in-sentence silences.
